title: SLI Sentinel: cross-region per-token latency normalization, failover signaling, and adaptive shed controller
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a lightweight SLI Sentinel service and dashboard panels that compute normalized, per-token latency SLIs across models and regions, produce deviation alerts for multi-region divergence, and emit actuating signals to the circuit manager and adaptive load-shed controller. The Sentinel will normalize latency by model profile and sequence-length distribution, correlate with KV cache hit rates and batch size distributions, and provide human-readable evidence for on-call runbooks and automated mitigation (shadow -> soft-shed -> hard-shed).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel service receives sampled token-level spans and produces normalized p50/p95/p99 SLIs per model-region within 30s of ingestion
Dashboard surfaces region delta panels and automatic anomaly flags; can filter by model, deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), and sequence-length bucket
Integration with circuit manager: Sentinel events map to circuit state transitions in the orchestration log and can trigger soft-shed policies in staging
Shadow mode in prod for 14 days with no traffic impact; enforcement rollout plan documented and validated
End-to-end tests: synthetic workload demonstrates graceful degradation sequence (shadow -> early-exit -> shed) and shows SLO recovery within target window
tasks: Design SLI normalization formula (model baseline + seq-length bucket weights) and document trade-offs
Implement Sentinel ingestion pipeline (Kafka -> Flink/Beam job -> timeseries store) and batch-aware aggregation
Add KV cache and batch-size correlation tags to ingest pipeline and create join reducers
Create Grafana dashboard panels: normalized SLI heatmap, region delta timeline, circuit-state overlay, shed event list
Wire Sentinel alerts to PagerDuty playbook and circuit-manager API (RFC for signal format)
Run shadow pilot in us-west-2/us-east-1 for 14 days and gather false-positive/false-negative metrics
Rollout enforcement: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha: Kickoff meeting notes posted to Confluence (link below). Agreed to prioritize normalization by model x seq-length rather than by customer tier to avoid confounding signals.
